title: Supernova remnant NGC 2060
caption: The supernova remnant NGC 2060, imaged by ESO
celestial: NGC 2060 · constellation Dorado · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This picture shows NGC 2060, the aftermath of a supernova in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small galaxy near our own, about 170,000 light-years away. On our sky it lies in the direction of the constellation Dorado.
A supernova marks the violent death of a massive star. The explosion blasts heated matter out into the surrounding space at great speed, and what is left behind is called a supernova remnant.

ESO describes the remnant NGC 2060 as resplendent. Its host, the Large Magellanic Cloud, is a small companion of the Milky Way that appears in the direction of Dorado on our sky, so the remnant is the wreckage of a massive star in another galaxy rather than in our own.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (5.56 x 6.81 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 275 × 337 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The telescope, instrument, filters and color mapping for this ESO image aren't published.
understand.eye: The remnant is far too faint and distant to see with the eye. A telescope's long exposure is needed.
